# openaec-ui

Native Rust shell, theme tokens, typography, semantic icons and controls shared by OpenAEC desktop tools. Implement `Application` and call `run`, or use `frame::FrameSlots` from an existing Iced event loop.

`design` holds the UI 0.4 design tokens, the start of library 0.4: the five themes (`ThemeId`: Licht, Donker, Blueprint, High contrast donker and High contrast licht), 31 opaque colour roles per theme, shadows, overlay, type, spacing, radii, shell sizes and the Werkruimte and Statusbalk settings (`ThemeTokens::palette`). `design::tokens` is generated from `design/ontwerp-0.4/tokens-0.4.json` by `scripts/generate_tokens_04.py`; do not edit it by hand. `design::widgets` draws the decided 0.4 components with those tokens only: buttons (primary, secondary, quiet, danger; regular and compact), icon buttons with tooltips, text fields with an error message, select lists, checkboxes, radio buttons, switches, sliders, progress bars, panels with a mono header, tree rows, the property grid, tables, in-page notifications (optionally with an action button), toasts, dialogs with the theme overlay, ribbon tabs with the Bestand button, large and small ribbon buttons, ribbon groups, document tabs (optionally pinned, without a close button), the status bar and the empty state. Every component takes a `design::Look` (theme plus Werkruimte and Statusbalk settings) and B2 icon sources, which `widgets::glyph` recolours per state. iced 0.14 has no dashed borders, so High contrast draws disabled borders solid; text fields and select lists show their focus as a 2 px inner border, while every other control gets the 2 px ring 2 px outside it from `design::focus` (in the 32 px title bar its top and bottom are clipped). `design::tiles` adds the tiles and cards (icon tile, task tile, recent files, project card with preview and status label, choice tile, info card, figure tile and the Bestand navigation row) and `design::workflow` the navigation of workflow apps: the 220 px sidebar, the 44 px step bar, the 52 px action bar and the `Navigation` setting. `design::chrome` holds the window chrome: the 32 px title bar with quick actions and window buttons (`WindowActions`; the application turns them into `iced::window` tasks), the panel splitter, and menus with icons, shortcuts, check marks, separators and a danger line, shown at the cursor by `menu_layer`. The rest of this crate is the earlier prototype and still uses its own `Theme`.

Keyboard (issue #2): every button, tile, tab, tree row, table row, menu item and choice in `design` takes part in the Tab route through `design::focus::focusable`; Enter and Space press the focused control, and the 2 px focus ring only shows when the focus came from the keyboard. Apps subscribe to `keyboard::navigation()` and answer with `keyboard::navigate(step)`, which wraps at both ends. Wrap the screen behind an open dialog or menu in `design::focus::inert(screen, true)`: Tab stays in the dialog and the focus returns to the same control when it closes. The close button of `widgets::dialog` stays out of the route, as Escape closes the dialog. `design::focus::group(content, Axis)` makes a list, menu, table, tab row, ribbon or sidebar one Tab stop that the arrow keys walk through (Home and End go to the ends); the library uses it in all of these, and apps wrap their own lists, such as a tree, the same way. `design::focus::expander(row, expanded, on_toggle)` lets Right open and Left close a tree branch while its row has the focus. `design::focus::tip(content, tip)` shows `tip` under `content` while a control inside has the keyboard focus, not after a click; Escape hides it until the focus moves on, and only that first Escape is taken (issue #7). `widgets::with_tooltip` uses it next to the hover tooltip, so every icon button's name and shortcut can be read without a mouse. iced 0.14 cannot end text with an ellipsis, so `widgets::shorten(text, max)` cuts it at a word with "…": document tabs shorten titles longer than `TAB_TITLE_MAX` (28) characters and table cells that do not fit a fixed column, and both show the full text as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. In Hoog contrast the selected table row and tree row carry a 2 px border instead of a tint and bar (issue #6); iced draws everything itself, so the Windows contrast themes do not change a Rust app.

Commands (issue #9): describe each command once as a `design::command::Command` (id, label, 16 and 24 px icon, `Shortcut`, kind: action, toggle, mode or dialog, and the message) and draw it with `command::ribbon_large`, `ribbon_small`, `icon_button`, `button` or `menu_item`, so the ribbon, menus, title bar and tooltips always show the same label, state and shortcut. Subscribe to `keyboard::presses()` and look each press up with `command::find(&commands, key, modifiers)`: a shortcut shown in a menu is then always a real binding. `command::conflicts` lists two commands with the same key; test that it is empty.

Own shortcuts (issue #22): `design::shortcuts::Keymap` holds only the shortcuts someone changed, by command id, and is saved as JSON at `shortcuts::keymap_path(app)` (`%APPDATA%\OpenAEC\<app>\sneltoetsen.json` on Windows). Apply it to the app's command list with `keymap.apply(&mut commands)`, and every ribbon button, menu item, tooltip and key follows. `shortcuts::page` is the Sneltoetsen page for the settings dialog: search, change by pressing the new keys (Backspace clears, Esc stops; navigation keys and plain letters are refused), a conflict question with Wisselen or Annuleren, and back to the default per command or for all. While `Editor::recording()` is true, send key presses to the page as `shortcuts::Message::Key` instead of running commands.

Characters (issue #25): `fonts::AEC_TEST_SET` lists the characters every OpenAEC font must show (⌀, m², ±, ≤, Greek, Ĳ, Turkish letters and look-alikes such as I/l/1). Inter lacks ⌀, Space Grotesk lacks Greek and JetBrains Mono lacks Ĳ; `fonts::install_fallback()` makes those come from the bundled Noto Sans and Noto Sans Symbols on every computer instead of a system font. `runtime::run` calls it; an application with its own `iced::application` calls it once before the first frame. cosmic-text only falls back to a face of exactly the requested weight, so each Noto face is registered for every weight. `scripts/check_font_glyphs.py` checks the fonts against the test set. `fonts::load_variable(bytes, weights)` loads a variable font unchanged and registers it for the given weights, so iced draws them from the `wght` axis; the font specimen in the gallery (issue #29) uses it for candidates whose licence forbids renaming a modified version.

Reports (issue #26): `report_fonts` gives every report and PDF export the same files as the interface. `report_fonts::font(Role)` picks the file per role: Inter Regular for body text, Inter SemiBold for emphasis and table headers, Space Grotesk Medium for headings, Space Grotesk Bold for the title, Inter AEC for columns of numbers and JetBrains Mono for codes. Inter's digits differ in width, and PDF writers do not apply OpenType features such as tabular figures, so number columns use Inter AEC: Inter with `tnum` and `ss04` frozen into the character map (issue #28, `scripts/build_inter_aec.py`). `fonts::NUMBERS` uses it in the interface too, for table numbers, number fields and totals. Each `ReportFont` carries its bytes, PostScript name and OFL text; the fonts have no Reserved Font Name, so embedding a subset is allowed. `report_fonts::runs(text, role)` splits text into pieces with one font each, sending ⌀, Greek in headings and Ĳ in codes to the Noto fallback, because PDF writers do not fall back themselves. `scripts/check_report_pdf.py` checks a finished PDF: every font embedded, the embedded data the font the PDF names, TrueType data not declared as Type1, and the font from this package.

Numbers (issue #8): `design::number` reads every number field the same way. A `NumberFormat` sets the decimals, the decimal sign (comma by default, `point()` for English), a unit, a minimum, a maximum and whether the field may be empty. `number::parse` only accepts a text that is the whole number: with a decimal comma, a point or space separates thousands in groups of three (`1.234,5`), `1.5` is refused with an explanation, more decimals than allowed are refused rather than rounded, and the unit may follow the number. `NumberInput` keeps the draft text as typed and returns a value only when it is valid, so an unfinished entry such as `1,` is neither an error nor stored. `number::number_field` draws the field with its unit and the error below it; `number::Value` also covers Gemengd and Onbekend. `widgets::property_row` now grows for such an error and keeps its label beside the field.

Saving and closing (issue #10): `design::document` keeps the bookkeeping every app needs, the app does the writing. `DocumentState` counts revisions: `edit()` for each change, `request(SaveKind)` hands out a `SaveTicket` for the revision on screen, and `finish(ticket, result)` marks only that revision as written, so an edit made during a save keeps the document unsaved. One write runs per document; a save asked meanwhile is queued and `finish` returns its ticket. `SaveKind::Autosave` needs a file name (`Request::NeedsPath` otherwise), and `SaveKind::Recovery` writes a recovery copy to `recovery_dir(app)` that never counts as saved. `ClosePlan` handles closing tabs or the window: it asks about each changed document in turn (`Step::Ask` with number and total), waits for the saves the person chose, and closes only when all are done; a failed save stops it. `document::close_dialog` draws the question with the same wording in every app.

Undo (issue #34): `design::history::History<S>` keeps one document's undo and redo as snapshots with a name per step. `record(label, before)` is one step; `record_merged(label, key, before)` folds a run of typing in one field into one step until `seal()` or another step, so Ctrl+Z first takes back the whole field edit (iced 0.14 text fields have no undo of their own); `begin`/`end(changed)` make a drag or bulk action one step, and `cancel()` hands back the state from before it. `undo(current)` and `redo(current)` return the state to show, and `undo_label()`/`redo_label()` with `history::undo_text` give "Ongedaan maken: Prijs wijzigen" for the menu and tooltip, set on the command with the new `Command::detail`. Each document has its own history; views of the same data share it. Actions outside the document (export, print, send) are not recorded, and their dialog says `history::IRREVERSIBLE`.

Accessible names (issue #3): iced 0.14 passes nothing to a screen reader yet, so `design::a11y` records now what one will need. Every control in `design` carries an `a11y::Node` with a `Role`, a name, a value, a description and its state (checked, selected, current, disabled, invalid), taken from its own label: buttons, checkboxes, switches, radios, tabs, tree rows, table rows (named by their cells), menu items, ribbon buttons (a toggle while on), tiles, sidebar and step items, dialogs (by title), banners and toasts (alert or status) and the status bar. Controls without text take a required name: `widgets::icon_button(look, icon, size, selected, name, on_press)` and `chrome::title_button(look, icon, selected, name, on_press)`; `command::icon_button` uses the command's text and shortcut. A select, slider or field gets its name from the label beside it: `widgets::property_row` wraps its value in a `Role::Label` node. Name your own controls with `a11y::named(control, role, name)` or `a11y::node(control, Node::new(..))`, around the focusable control. `a11y::Collect` is an operation that gathers the nodes of a screen and lists every control in the Tab route without a name; a node names the controls within its bounds unless it is a container (group, dialog, alert, status). Test with it that every control is named, as the gallery does for every view. A bridge to AccessKit can read the same nodes once iced supports it (issue #5).

Updates (issue #33): the OpenAEC Installer is the one place for updates; apps only report them. The installer writes a status file (`update::status_path()`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAEC\installer\updates.json` on Windows) with its own path and, per app by its catalogue id such as `open-calc-studio`, the latest version and release page. `update::check_installed(app_id, env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))` reads it at start and returns an `Available` when the listed version is newer (`update::compare` handles `2026.44.1`, `v1.10.0` and suffixes). Put `update::notice(look, &available, Message::Update)` in the `extra` part of the title bar: "Versie … staat klaar" and a compact "Bijwerken" button. On that message, close through a `document::ClosePlan` first, so no work is lost, and when it finishes call `update::open_installer(&available)`, which starts `<installer> --update <app id>`, or opens the https release page when no installer is found, and then close the window. Apps never download or install anything themselves.

Text size (issue #27): every `Look` carries a Tekstgrootte, `TextSize::Compact`, `Standard` (the default, the 0.4 sizes) or `Large`. `look.text` holds the sizes for that setting (`label`, `body`, `panel_heading`, `dialog_heading`, `page_heading`) and the height of rows with text (`row`: 24, 28 or 32 px), and every component in `design` uses them, so use `look.text.*` instead of `font::SIZE_*` in an app too. Set it with `Look::new(..).with_text_size(size)`. Icons stay at 16 and 24 px, so they stay sharp. `design::display::Display` keeps theme, Werkruimte, Statusbalk and Tekstgrootte per app as JSON at `display::settings_path(app)` (`%APPDATA%\OpenAEC\<app>\weergave.json`, next to the shortcuts); `Display::look()` gives the look. The standard application `blueprint` saves it on every change.

Website style (issue #13): `design::site` draws the style of open-aec.com for the OpenAEC Installer, the hub app of proposal E (`design/ontwerp-0.4/05-layouts.md`). It holds the tile surfaces `card_style`, `glass_card_style` and `glass_style`, the dark top band `dark_band_style(band_look(look))`, the buttons `button` and `small_button` with `Kind::Primary`, `Light` or `Glass`, the 34 px `round_icon` with a tooltip that also shows on keyboard focus, `icon_tile`, `section_label`, `section_head`, `chip` and the filter `pill`, plus `HEADING_BOLD`, `gradient` and `alpha`. Everything is drawn with the 0.4 tokens: the primary button keeps dark text on amber for contrast, and in High contrast gradients, glows and glass give way to plain surfaces and 2 px borders. Every control carries its `a11y::Node`. Other apps keep the standard shell; this style is for the hub only.

For a Frame Studio-style workspace, use `frame::workspace_frame` with `WorkspaceFrameSlots` and `WorkspaceFrameProfile::OPEN_FRAME`. This optional shell keeps the reviewed 36 px title and 28 px status bands, lets the ribbon and workspace tabs grow when they wrap, and places the application content between them. `frame::workspace_panes` supplies the reviewed 220/290 px default side widths when those panels are visible; the application may copy the profile and replace widths with persisted values. `status_bar_with_height` supplies the shared status treatment at the 28 px height. The [source comparison](../../design/frame-layout-review.html) records the measured Svelte geometry and contrast decisions. This is a reusable shell API, not yet a Frame Studio application migration.

For sidebar-first tools without a ribbon, `frame::sidebar_frame` and `SidebarFrameProfile::WORKSPACE_COMPOSER` provide the source-measured 32 px title, 220 px sidebar, and 22 px status bands. `ChromeMode::SidebarCompact` uses this frame in the shared runtime and passes the application's navigation through `Application::explorer` without adding a generic panel heading. The Style Repo's Workspace Composer review exercises Simple/Advanced navigation and all 18 pinned routes. Its package and preset cards are review interactions, not an installer backend or a pixel-matched migration.

`ChromeMode::ThreePaneFixed { left_width, right_width }` gives source-specific tools exact native pane widths while retaining the shared ribbon, document and status bands. The Calc screen review uses 320/240 px to reproduce the panel widths visible in the pinned Dutch capture; `App.tsx` initializes the left panel at 220 px, so this is a capture-state choice, not a changed Calc default.

`frame::status_bar` owns the shared 22 px status band, one-pixel top rule, theme colors and horizontal padding. An existing application supplies its own status cells and actions as an Iced `Element`; the same component is used by the Style Repo shell and Pointcloud Studio.

`widgets::title_action` owns the 30 × 26 px quick-access control, hover color and tooltip for the title strip. The Style Repo and Pointcloud supply their own command icons, labels and messages through this same Rust widget.

`widgets::themed_tooltip` owns the 12 px label, 8 × 12 px padding, 340 px maximum width and 8 px gap for ribbon, panel and status controls. The Style Repo ribbon and Pointcloud controls use this same tooltip; follow-cursor tips can override the gap.

`widgets::settings_modal` owns the source Style Book's 560 × 500 px settings chrome, 120 px sidebar, overlay, header and footer. Each app supplies its own tabs and settings fields. The backdrop does not dismiss the dialog, matching the pinned Tauri template.
`widgets::dialog_modal` owns the source Style Book's general modal: an application-selected width, 30 px header, square border, content surface, 44 px footer and inert full-window overlay. The source reset confirmation uses it at 340 px; Pointcloud's 2D drawing dialog and the Style Repo's interactive sample use it at 480 px. `Application::overlay` places domain dialogs above the complete shared shell, and `Application::escape` gives them Escape handling after the shared settings dialog.
The header uses the source top-to-bottom theme gradient, and `Theme::dialog_shadow` supplies its 0 × 4 px, 16 px-blur shadow in all five themes. The general and settings modals share these treatments.
Both modal variants are centered initially, can be dragged by the 30 px header without stealing the close button, stay within the application window, and cap their height at 90% of the viewport. The settings body scrolls when this cap reduces the available space.
`widgets::settings_tab` gives those tabs the same square 11 px navigation style. The crate shell provides selectable General, Appearance and About pages; other applications can supply their own page content and messages.
`widgets::settings_theme_picker` provides the 200 px trigger and anchored overlay menu with five choices and four 14 px swatches per row. It closes on an outside click without changing form layout. `Theme::swatches` is the single source of those colors for Style Repo and Pointcloud. Both apps own selection and preview behavior; the native review renders deliberately show the menu expanded.
`widgets::settings_reset_confirmation` renders the 340 px reset prompt above the settings modal. The crate shell previews theme, language and scale until Save; Cancel restores the values from when the dialog opened. Reset changes the preview only after confirmation. The shared runtime writes the preferences file on Save.

`frame::document_bar` owns the 30 px document band from the pinned Tauri Style Book: the one-pixel top and bottom rules, theme background and 4 px horizontal inset. Applications keep their own tab identity and navigation behavior.

`widgets::document_tab_style` and `widgets::document_close_style` give those app-owned tabs the shared 24 px appearance and a legible close action. Pointcloud retains its middle-click, shortening, scrolling and keyboard behavior while using the same visual tab styles as the Style Repo.

`widgets::ribbon_group` owns the 94 px ribbon-group geometry from the pinned Tauri template: 4 px top inset, 8 px sides, a ruled 9 px caption and a right separator. Applications pass their actual tools and measured group width. Pointcloud keeps its adaptive collapse and domain actions; the Style Repo uses the same group around its catalogue commands.

`model::RibbonControl` adds typed ribbon inputs to `Command`: a slider, a two-thumb range, a compact stack of sliders, segmented choices, select lists, numeric text input, compact labelled form stacks with number, select and slider rows, a color choice and a style gallery. Applications own the selected values and receive changes through their message type; `widgets::ribbon_control` draws the controls with the shared tokens. The range widget keeps both handles on one rail and supports mouse and touch dragging. Select lists accept application-owned labels, messages and width; slider stacks accept source-specific labels and icons within the same ribbon geometry. The color choice shows the current application color even when it came from a style preset outside the listed palette. `RibbonSwatch` carries a labelled color preview, an optional dashed border and an application message, so the gallery contains no PDF-specific meaning. The gallery shows an application-selected number of tiles and provides an aligned popup for the full set.

`widgets::color_grid` renders an app-owned palette in vertical columns with keyboard-focusable color buttons and tooltips. `widgets::popover` and `widgets::popover_aligned` anchor arbitrary app content over the shell, moves it above the anchor when there is insufficient room below, and closes on an outside click. `RibbonCustomColor` lets an application supply a validated custom-color editor inside the same popup. The Style Repo uses them together in the PDF ribbon; a software-rendered pixel test checks all 42 source colors in their 7 × 6 arrangement, and an event test checks palette actions and outside-click dismissal.

`widgets::backstage_nav_with` draws the shared 260 px File navigation with 40 px page rows, a selected accent mark, separators and Settings/Back/Exit footer. Applications provide translated pages, enabled actions and a theme resolver. The Style Repo shell uses it for catalogue navigation and hides its ribbon and document band while File is open; Pointcloud uses the same component for its seven real file pages. Pointcloud also anchors its Display controls with `popover_aligned`.

`backstage_page_heading`, `backstage_group_caption`, `backstage_task_tile_with` and `backstage_tile_column` draw the reusable File-page content rhythm. The tile column is limited to 620 px; each tile owns title/detail typography, a 4 px border and enabled/disabled/hover colours, while applications supply translated content and actions. Pointcloud uses these for its New, Open, Import and Export tasks; the Style Repo components page shows enabled and disabled examples.

`widgets::form_field` provides a labelled, application-owned input for full-page screens; the Style Repo uses it in the native Field Project form. `widgets::property_grid_row_with`, `property_grid_control_with`, and `property_section_with` provide the shared properties dock. Rows are 28 px high with aligned label and value columns and a bottom rule; section headers are 24 px high. Callers supply their own localized text, input controls and theme resolver. The Style Repo shows a live scale slider in the control grid; Pointcloud uses the same rows for its six section-box sliders and editable layout viewport fields.

`find_bar::view` draws a native document search overlay from the pinned PDF Studio FindBar, with its five verified UI SVGs, 24 px input, 22 px navigation buttons and source filters. Pass the document viewport width so options move to a second row below 370 px; the application owns query, results, navigation and keyboard shortcuts through `FindBarState` and `FindBarActions`. The Style Repo's Components page and standalone example have interactive samples and a [software-rendered review](../../design/pdf-find-bar-screen-review.html); the Pointcloud snapshot includes the component for future use.

This package contains the shared Rust implementation, nine bundled fonts (Inter AEC among them) and two Noto fallback fonts with their [separate license notices](NOTICE.md) and a [font manifest](assets/fonts/manifest.json) listing family, weight, version, SHA-256 and licence per file, 35 canonical control icons including the source-reviewed Speech microphone and the Geotechniek-reviewed Print, Save As and Restore commands, and 36 reviewed domain meanings with separate 16 px artwork: four from CAD/Pointcloud, three geotechnical placement symbols, four drawing/transform commands shared by Geotechniek and Pointcloud, five CAD editing commands reviewed against Geotechniek and OpenCAD, three Geotechniek drawing/frame commands, two Pointcloud drawing-annotation commands (Text and Leader), and fifteen PDF ribbon meanings reviewed against seven source icon collisions. `icons::DomainIcon` and `model::CommandIcon::Domain` keep those commands distinct from the general `icons::Icon` set. `Icon::Settings` is a gear for app settings; `Icon::Controls` retains the slider symbol for view/property controls. The 32 `ribbon_icons::RibbonIcon` variants carry source-used Style Book Tauri ribbon vectors with distinct command meanings. Applications still supply their own command behavior and screens. Source icons collected for design research, unapproved FEM/BIM drafts and Style Repo screenshots live in the sibling `openaec-style-repo` application and are not included in this crate package.

The PDF meanings distinguish Fit Width, Actual Size, Edit Text, Clear Page, Delete Page, Single Page, Continuous Pages, File Association, Book View, Shortcuts, Navigation, Manage Watermarks, Proofread and Split Document. Fit Page, Find, and Text Annotation reuse `Icon::Fit`, `Icon::Search`, and `DomainIcon::DrawingText`. Seven PDF meanings have separate optically simplified 16 px vectors, including IFC report export, which combines a cube with an outgoing arrow missing from the source UI icon. Proofread and Split Document follow reviewed, actually used ribbon commands in public PDF main `ae1d787`; the compare split-mode illustration is not part of this command API. These semantics are available to tools through the crate, but the original PDF Studio JavaScript application has not been migrated.

The [private OpenAEC Blueprint repository](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/OpenAEC-Blueprint) is the canonical Git source for this crate. Pointcloud carries a verified local snapshot so its public checkout remains buildable without private repository access; run `python3 scripts/check_portable_ui.py` from the Style Repo to check source and asset parity. The sibling Style Repo application documents the source inventory and the Pointcloud integration.
